name: Burgenwelt Ehrenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Burgenwelt Ehrenberg near Reutte unites four monumental hilltop fortresses, the interactive Knights Museum, and the dizzying highline179 pedestrian suspension bridge.
preis: Valley Klause and castle ruins freely accessible; Museum and highline179 require tickets
oeffnungszeiten: Castle ruins open year-round; museum and highline179 open daily
beschreibung:
Überblick

The monumental Burgenwelt Ehrenberg near Reutte in the Tyrolean Außerfern region ranks among Central Europe's most significant and historically evocative fortification ensembles. Commandingly erected along the ancient Via Claudia Augusta trade highway traversing the Fern Pass, this strategic stronghold controlled commerce and troop movements between Bavaria and the Italian peninsula for centuries. The sprawling heritage landmark comprises four interconnected defense works spanning different architectural epochs: the late-medieval Klause valley toll station, the imposing 13th-century Burgruine Ehrenberg citadel crowning the hillside, the 18th-century baroque fortress Schlosskopf on the summit ridge, and the opposing Fort Claudia. In recent years, a world-famous engineering marvel linked two of the strongholds: the dramatic pedestrian suspension bridge highline179, dangling 114 metres above the B179 highway across an awe-inspiring span of 406 metres.

Route & Anforderungen

The fortress landscape offers walking itineraries suited to every fitness level. From the valley Klause complex, visitors reach the central Ehrenberg ruins and the highline179 either via a scenic forested gravel path (approx. 30 minutes walk, 110 metres elevation gain) or effortlessly via the barrier-free 'Ehrenberg Liner' inclined funicular elevator. Hikers seeking the summit view can continue ascending the fortifications to the Schlosskopf redoubt (an additional 45 minutes, 150 vertical metres, sturdy hiking shoes required). Solid footwear with treaded soles is strongly recommended for navigating historic stone stairs and unpaved pathways around the ruins. The experiential museum 'In the Footsteps of the Knight' in the valley is fully wheelchair-accessible.

Besuch & Anreise

Access by car is toll-free from Füssen and Kempten along highway B179, or from Innsbruck via the Fern Pass to the dedicated Burgenwelt Ehrenberg exit just south of Reutte. Generous paid parking lots for cars and touring coaches are situated directly at the Klause visitor center. Rail travelers take the scenic Außerfernbahn train to Reutte in Tirol station and transfer to regional bus routes heading towards Fernpass/Nassereith, alighting directly at the Ehrenberger Klause bus stop.

Tipps

Crossing the suspension bridge highline179 requires a steady head for heights, but rewards daring walkers with unforgettable thrill and sweeping vistas over the valley basin of Reutte. When visiting with children, do not miss the interactive museum in the Klause, where young adventurers can try on genuine medieval helmets and handle knightly chainmail.
